rows.grounds: Indeclinable indicating the contrary condition to the prescribed guru-worship and offering.
Predicate describing the result when the prescribed conditions are not met.
Refers to all ritual efforts undertaken without proper guru-worship and dakṣiṇā.
Compound of koṭi (ten million) and puraścaraṇa (preliminary rite); instrumental of means, contrasted as ineffective.
Rhetorical interrogative implying futility despite vast ritual effort.

items.question: Why are even vast preliminary rites rendered futile without proper worship and offerings to the guru?
premises: Proper worship of the guru brings ritual completeness.
Proper offerings to the guru are required as part of that worship.
Without these, all ritual efforts become fruitless.
items.inference: Therefore, even ten million preliminary rites are of no use if proper guru-worship and offerings are neglected.
uncertainties: The exact scope of 'sarvaṃ' (all rites or all results) is contextually inferred from the preceding verses.
items.plain_english: Otherwise, everything is fruitless; what is the use of even ten million preliminary rites?
